prize_parts.citation: For the development of ionizable lipid nanoparticles as a chemical platform for delivering nucleic-acid medicines
For the development of base editing, the chemical conversion of single DNA bases without double-strand cleavage

statement.case_for: I propose two distinct achievements. Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are a clean case of molecular design: pH-switchable lipids that are neutral in circulation and cationic in the endosome solved the delivery bottleneck for siRNA and mRNA. Billions of vaccine doses and approved siRNA drugs leave no doubt about maturity or impact, and the 2023 Medicine prize honoured the cargo but not the carrier. Base editing is a rationally engineered chemical transformation, deaminase chemistry on a programmable DNA scaffold, with a clear intellectual driver in Liu, independent reproduction in many labs and clinical results arriving. In my opening I put prime editing (B061) first. Having read the colleagues' arguments I now think base editing is the better-matured and more broadly supported genome-editing achievement, and the one for which a Liu-only attribution is cleanest. Together the two parts keep the prize within three people and combine a physical-organic design story with a protein-engineering story.
statement.case_against: Both parts sit close to biology and medicine, and the 2020 CRISPR prize and the 2023 mRNA prize both lie nearby, so the committee could judge that each is already half-recognised. The LNP attribution is the weaker part: Cullis, Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer all have real claims, patent disputes colour the record, and any two or three names will leave out people whose contributions were foundational. Base editing is under a decade old, and long-term clinical safety is not established. The Kondo and Nishida deaminase work is a separate line that a Liu-only citation does not acknowledge. Against my own configuration, targeted protein degradation has the broadest opening support and arguably the most chemical novelty, and I rank it behind these only because of attribution and clinical maturity.

responses.point: Targeted protein degradation (B063) should be first: it turns small molecules into programmable effectors of ubiquitin-mediated proteolysis, and Crews, Deshaies and Handa are the decisive names.
responses.response: I agree that the concept is original and chemically rich, and I do not dismiss it. My difficulty is attribution. The PROTAC concept (Crews, Deshaies), the cereblon and molecular-glue mechanism (Handa, Ito) and the structure-based VHL work (Ciulli) are three strands, and the shortlist names eight people. A three-person cut would exclude Ciulli and Gray, who made the approach drug-like. The first approved degrader is also still pending. I would support B063 if the committee can agree on a defensible mechanism-centred citation, but I do not yet see that. It is my first alternative after the preferred pair.

responses.point: Ionizable-lipid nanoparticles (B035) belong first, as physical chemistry of lipid self-assembly and non-bilayer phase behaviour, credited to Cullis, Hope and Madden.
responses.response: I agree that this is the right frame, and we are close on the science. Our disagreement is over names. Your Vancouver triple is historically coherent for the formulation science. I credited Cullis with Anderson because the lipidoid and combinatorial route is what carried the lipids into approved siRNA and mRNA products, and because Anderson is not tied to the Vancouver patent disputes. I would value hearing whether you think Hope and Madden's lipid-assembly work outweighs the translation route, because that decides how the credit should be split. I do not think a three-person LNP part leaves room for a second achievement.

responses.point: Massively parallel sequencing (B031) is the chemistry of reversible terminators and surface clustering, credited to Balasubramanian and Klenerman, and is timely to overdue.
responses.response: The maturity case is the strongest of any candidate and I accept it. My reservation is about boundaries. Sanger sequencing was recognised in 1980, and Rothberg's pyrosequencing, Ju's terminators and Mayer's clustering are parallel contributions to the same outcome. The credit is also not as clean as a two-person prize implies. I would place it just below my pair as a fully legitimate chemistry prize, and I would not oppose it as a second part beside the genome-editing or delivery work if the committee prefers a more analytical-chemistry flavour.

responses.point: Proton-coupled electron transfer (B025) is a unifying principle across respiration, photosynthesis and water oxidation, with Mayer, Hammes-Schiffer and Nocera as the decisive trio.
responses.response: I agree on the scientific stature and on maturity. PCET has been confirmed over decades and it matters for enzyme mechanism. What gives me pause is breadth. It is a principle that cuts across several fields, and the credit is spread over four named people plus a long tail of theory and experiment. Meyer's claim is as strong as that of anyone in the trio. That makes a precise citation hard to write, though not impossible. I think it is a serious candidate for a later year, and I would back it over several others if the committee wants a physical or inorganic chemistry prize.

responses.point: Rational design of zeolites and molecular sieves (B051) is mature, industrially huge and linked to Corma, Davis and Zones, with no risk of being premature.
responses.response: I accept the industrial and chemical weight, and I fully agree that there is no maturity risk. The difficulty is that the field is broad and the decisive credit is diffuse, with Yu, Tsapatsis and others also named. I also noted that porous frameworks were recently recognised, in the 2025 MOF prize, and the committee may feel that the porous-materials area has just been addressed. I would not rank it above the pair I propose, but I do not rule it out in a later year.

uncertainties: Whether Anderson or Hope/Madden is the right second or third name for the lipid nanoparticle part, and whether any LNP citation can avoid patent-dispute entanglement.
Whether the committee prefers base editing (B068) or prime editing (B061) as the genome-editing part, and whether a Liu-only award is acceptable given Komor, Gaudelli, Anzalone, Nishida and Kondo.
Whether the committee will see delivery and genome editing as chemistry rather than medicine.
Whether targeted protein degradation will become the majority choice and what attribution can be agreed for it.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile for the shortlisted candidates. My postdoc with Arieh Warshel concerns EVB and enzyme simulation, and he is not named on any shortlisted ballot. My computational interests touch proton-coupled electron transfer theory (B025, Hammes-Schiffer) only at a field level, which I do not consider a recusal issue.
